story: NSF opens the State and Regional AI Infrastructure Hubs program and caps every state at one award, so Alaska's whole claim on it is a single application due November 4, 2026

claims.claim: NSF solicitation 26-513 states that only one award per state or multi-state region will be made.
claims.verbatim: Only one award per state or multi-state region will be made.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. National Science Foundation, Program Solicitation NSF 26-513
claims.notes: SPINE CLAIM. Verified across three independent fetches of the solicitation page, each returning the sentence character for character. The sentence appears twice, in the Important Information block and again under Award Information. Corroborated independently by NSF's own announcement, see C02.

claims.claim: NSF's announcement says it will initially support up to 10 AI Infrastructure Hubs with one award made per state or region.
claims.value: up to 10 hubs, one per state
claims.verbatim: NSF will initially support up to 10 AI Infrastructure Hubs, with one award made per state or region.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. National Science Foundation news release
claims.notes: Second, independent NSF surface for the one-per-state rule in C01. Note the announcement says state or region while the solicitation says state or multi-state region. Use the solicitation wording when the exact phrase matters.

claims.claim: The solicitation says an institution may appear as a participant in at most one proposal.
claims.verbatim: An institution may appear as a participant in at most one proposal.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. National Science Foundation, Program Solicitation NSF 26-513
claims.notes: SPINE CLAIM. Verified verbatim on three fetches.

claims.claim: The solicitation says that if more than one proposal contains an institution as a participant then only the first one will be reviewed.
claims.verbatim: If more than one proposal contains an institution as a participant then only the first one will be reviewed. All others will be returned without review.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. National Science Foundation, Program Solicitation NSF 26-513
claims.notes: SPINE CLAIM. The second sentence, All others will be returned without review, appeared on the first and second fetches. It is the enforcement half of C03 and is what makes a duplicate listing costly rather than merely disallowed.

claims.claim: The solicitation prohibits inclusion of voluntary committed cost sharing.
claims.verbatim: Inclusion of voluntary committed cost sharing is prohibited.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. National Science Foundation, Program Solicitation NSF 26-513
claims.notes: SPINE CLAIM. Verified verbatim on three fetches, and it is the only sentence on the page containing the phrase cost sharing. SOFTENING REQUIRED. This bars an applicant from VOLUNTARILY pledging matching funds inside the proposal. It is standard NSF boilerplate and it is not a ban on a state spending its own money on compute. Deck copy must say the solicitation bars a proposer from pledging extra money into the proposal, not that Alaska is forbidden to spend on compute.

claims.claim: The full proposal deadline for the first cycle of NSF 26-513 is November 4, 2026.
claims.verbatim: November 04, 2026
claims.source_outlet: U.S. National Science Foundation, Program Solicitation NSF 26-513
claims.notes: SPINE CLAIM. Printed on the page as November 04, 2026 in the Full Proposal Deadline block, confirmed on two fetches. The NSF news release of August 4th does NOT carry the deadline, so this claim rests on the solicitation alone, which is the primary document. Prose should render it November 4, 2026 or November 4th.

claims.claim: There are 82 days from the run date of August 14, 2026 to the November 4, 2026 full proposal deadline.
claims.verbatim: November 04, 2026
claims.source_outlet: U.S. National Science Foundation, Program Solicitation NSF 26-513
claims.notes: DERIVED. Arithmetic, re-derivable. August 14th to August 31st is 17 days. All of September is 30. All of October is 31. November 1st to November 4th is 4. 17 plus 30 plus 31 plus 4 equals 82. Deadline date from C06. If the deck ships on a later date the figure must be recomputed.

claims.claim: NSF's solicitation says access to AI infrastructure including computing, data and software is highly uneven across the nation.
claims.verbatim: Today, access to this infrastructure is highly uneven across the nation.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. National Science Foundation, Program Solicitation NSF 26-513
claims.notes: SPINE CLAIM. This is NSF's stated problem, and it is what the one-award-per-state remedy in C01 has to be measured against. The referent of this infrastructure is the preceding sentence, which names computing, data and software. The grammatical slip in NSF's own sentence must not be silently corrected if quoted.

claims.claim: NSF's August 4th announcement says access to AI infrastructure remains highly uneven across the nation.
claims.verbatim: Today, access to AI infrastructure remains highly uneven across the nation.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. National Science Foundation news release
claims.notes: The announcement's wording differs from the solicitation's, see C08. If the deck puts either on a slide it must match the URL it cites. Do not blend them.

claims.claim: NSF's announcement describes the program as a $100 million initiative.
claims.verbatim: a $100 million initiative to drive AI-enabled scientific discovery and innovation across disciplines
claims.source_outlet: U.S. National Science Foundation news release
claims.notes: SOFTENING REQUIRED, and this is the run's sharpest numeric tension. The press release says $100 million flat. The solicitation's own Anticipated Funding Amount line says $40,000,000 to $100,000,000, see C11, so $100 million is the TOP of the stated range and not a committed floor. Preferred deck phrasing is NSF announced the program as a $100 million initiative, with the solicitation putting anticipated funding at $40 million to $100 million. Do not write NSF is spending $100 million.

claims.claim: The solicitation gives the anticipated funding amount for NSF 26-513 as $40,000,000 to $100,000,000.
claims.verbatim: Anticipated Funding Amount: $40,000,000 to $100,000,000
claims.source_outlet: U.S. National Science Foundation, Program Solicitation NSF 26-513
claims.notes: Returned identically on three fetches of the solicitation. The same page also carries the sentence Approximately $100,000,000 is available for this program, so the document states both a range and a headline figure. Both were confirmed present. Report the range as the solicitation's number and the $100 million as the announcement's, per C10. The page contains no sentence reading subject to the availability of funds, which was checked for explicitly and returned NOT PRESENT.

claims.claim: The solicitation anticipates 10 awards in each award cycle.
claims.verbatim: The program anticipates 10 awards in each award cycle.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. National Science Foundation, Program Solicitation NSF 26-513
claims.notes: The summary block also prints Estimated Number of Awards: 10. The announcement's phrasing is up to 10, see C02, which is the more cautious of the two. Sanity check on magnitudes. $100,000,000 divided by 10 is $10,000,000 per award, which sits inside the $4,000,000 to $12,000,000 band in C13. The numbers are internally consistent.

claims.claim: NSF anticipates typical proposals to the program will request 5 years and between $4,000,000 and $12,000,000 total budget.
claims.verbatim: NSF anticipates typical proposals to State and Regional AI Infrastructure Hubs Program should request 5 years and between $4,000,000 - $12,000,000 total budget.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. National Science Foundation, Program Solicitation NSF 26-513
claims.notes: SOFTENING REQUIRED. NSF's own verbs are anticipates and should request. This is guidance to proposers, not a hard cap on what an award can be. Preferred phrasing is NSF expects proposals to request $4 million to $12 million over 5 years. The source prints the range with a hyphen, which the deck renders as $4 million to $12 million per the house range rule.

claims.claim: The program's full official title is U.S. National Science Foundation State and Regional Artificial Intelligence Infrastructure Hubs, Expanding Access to Compute for Scientific Discovery.
claims.value: Expanding Access to Compute for Scientific Discovery
claims.verbatim: U.S. National Science Foundation State and Regional Artificial Intelligence Infrastructure Hubs: Expanding Access to Compute for Scientific Discovery (AI Infrastructure Hubs)
claims.source_outlet: U.S. National Science Foundation, Program Solicitation NSF 26-513
claims.notes: The official title contains a colon and the house rule bars a colon in claim text, so the claim sentence substitutes a comma. The verbatim field preserves NSF's punctuation exactly and is the string to set if the title is typeset on a slide. NSF's own short form is AI Infrastructure Hubs.

claims.claim: The solicitation is numbered NSF 26-513 and was posted on July 31, 2026.
claims.verbatim: Program Solicitation NSF 26-513
claims.source_outlet: U.S. National Science Foundation, Program Solicitation NSF 26-513
claims.notes: The posted date is printed on the page as Posted July 31, 2026, returned on the first fetch and consistent with the URL slug nsf26-513. The solicitation posting is four days before the run window opens and should be labelled as such if the date is shown.

claims.claim: NSF announced the State and Regional AI Infrastructure Hubs program on August 4, 2026.
claims.verbatim: New NSF State and Regional AI Infrastructure Hubs will power AI-enabled scientific research across the country
claims.source_outlet: U.S. National Science Foundation news release
claims.notes: The date line August 4, 2026 is printed on the page and was returned on both fetches. Inside the run window of August 4th to August 14th, on its opening day. The verbatim field holds the headline, which is the string that proves the announcement is the announcement.

claims.claim: Brian Stone, performing the duties of the NSF director, is the NSF official quoted in the announcement.
claims.verbatim: Brian Stone, performing the duties of the NSF director
claims.source_outlet: U.S. National Science Foundation news release
claims.notes: Title returned identically on both fetches. Render the title exactly as NSF gives it. He is not styled director, and calling him NSF director would be wrong.

claims.claim: Brian Stone said the program supports a national mission to advance AI for science by expanding access to critical AI resources.
claims.value: expanding access to critical AI resources
claims.verbatim: The State and Regional AI Infrastructure Hubs program supports a national mission to advance AI for science by expanding access to critical AI resources, strengthening state and regional ecosystems, and developing the workforce capabilities needed to harness these technologies.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. National Science Foundation news release
claims.notes: This is a 38 word EXCERPT from a longer quotation of roughly 85 words. The excerpt is contiguous and unaltered. If a slide sets it, no ellipsis is needed inside it, but the deck should not present it as the whole quote.

claims.claim: Michael Kratsios, assistant to the president and director of the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy, is also quoted in the NSF announcement.
claims.verbatim: American scientists deserve the world's best tools to enable their most ambitious work.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. National Science Foundation news release
claims.notes: Returned on the second, narrow fetch of the announcement and not surfaced on the first. Single fetch confirmation, so confidence is set below the Stone quote. Use only if the deck needs a second voice, and if used, quote exactly as given.

claims.claim: The solicitation names two categories of eligible proposers, institutions of higher education and non-profit non-academic organizations.
claims.verbatim: Institutions of Higher Education (IHEs): Two- and four-year IHEs (including community colleges) accredited in, and having a campus located in the U.S., acting on behalf of their faculty members.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. National Science Foundation, Program Solicitation NSF 26-513
claims.notes: The second bullet covers non-profit, non-academic organizations such as independent museums, observatories, research laboratories and professional societies located in the U.S. The complete list was requested explicitly on the third fetch and returned exactly two bullets. The page was also searched for the word Tribal, which returned NOT PRESENT, so Tribal colleges and Alaska Native organizations are not named as their own eligibility category. Do not assert that they are excluded, since an accredited Tribal college is an IHE. Assert only that the solicitation names no Tribal category.

claims.claim: The solicitation limits an individual to participating in at most one proposal as PI, co-PI or Senior or Key Personnel for each deadline.
claims.verbatim: An individual may participate in at most one State and Regional AI Infrastructure Hubs proposal as PI, co-PI, or Senior/Key Personnel for each deadline.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. National Science Foundation, Program Solicitation NSF 26-513
claims.notes: Returned on the second fetch only. Single confirmation, so confidence is lower than the institutional limit in C03. Corroborative of the deck's argument but not load bearing for it.

claims.claim: The solicitation lists subsequent full proposal deadlines of November 3, 2027 and the first Wednesday in November annually thereafter.
claims.verbatim: First Wednesday in November, Annually Thereafter
claims.source_outlet: U.S. National Science Foundation, Program Solicitation NSF 26-513
claims.notes: SOFTENING REQUIRED. The recurrence is what the solicitation says today and future cycles depend on appropriations. Sanity check on the dates. November 4, 2026 is a Wednesday and it is the first Wednesday of that month. November 3, 2027 is a Wednesday and the first Wednesday of that month. The stated pattern is internally consistent. Useful against the deck's argument, because a state that misses one cycle is not shut out forever, and the deck should not imply it is.

claims.claim: The U.S. Census Bureau puts Alaska's land area at 570,641 square miles, the largest of any state.
claims.verbatim: The table below provides land, water and total area measurements for the 50 states, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico and the Island Areas.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Census Bureau, State Area Measurements and Internal Point Coordinates
claims.notes: BACKGROUND, outside the run window by design. Both fetches of this page returned 570,641 square miles land area for Alaska and both confirmed it is the largest land area in the table. Total area is given as 665,384 square miles and water area as 94,743. Internal sanity check, 570,641 plus 94,743 equals 665,384, which reconciles exactly. The verbatim field carries the table's own caption because the figure itself lives in a table cell rather than in a sentence.

claims.claim: Alaska's land area is about 552 times Rhode Island's, and NSF 26-513 caps each of them at one award.
claims.verbatim: The table below provides land, water and total area measurements for the 50 states, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico and the Island Areas.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Census Bureau, State Area Measurements and Internal Point Coordinates
claims.notes: DERIVED. Arithmetic, re-derivable. Alaska land area 570,641 square miles divided by Rhode Island land area 1,034 square miles equals 551.88, which the deck states as about 552 times. Rhode Island's figures were confirmed on both fetches, land 1,034 and total 1,545. Rhode Island is the smallest state by land area in the same table. The cap half of the sentence rests on C01, not on Census. Both sides of the ratio use LAND area, deliberately.

claims.claim: A University of Alaska Fairbanks energy research project received a $725,000 award from the U.S. Department of Energy.
claims.verbatim: A new energy research project led by the University of Alaska Fairbanks has received a $725,000 award from the U.S. Department of Energy.
claims.source_outlet: University of Alaska Fairbanks
claims.notes: Sentence returned identically on both fetches. Inside the run window. UAF is the award recipient describing its own award, which is why this is marked primary, though it is not the DOE award notice itself. Used in this deck only as a scale comparator.

claims.claim: The smallest budget NSF says it anticipates for a hub proposal is about 5.5 times the whole AURORA-AI award to UAF.
claims.verbatim: NSF anticipates typical proposals to State and Regional AI Infrastructure Hubs Program should request 5 years and between $4,000,000 - $12,000,000 total budget.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. National Science Foundation, Program Solicitation NSF 26-513
claims.notes: DERIVED, and it spans two sources. Arithmetic, $4,000,000 from C13 divided by $725,000 from C25 equals 5.5172, stated as about 5.5 times. SOFTENING REQUIRED on two counts. The $4,000,000 is NSF's anticipated floor and not a guaranteed minimum, and the two awards are different agencies funding different things over different terms, so the comparison is one of scale only and must be labelled that way. Do not imply DOE underfunded UAF.

claims.claim: The UAF project is called AURORA-AI, short for Alaska Utility Resilience and Optimization using Real-time AI.
claims.verbatim: The AURORA-AI project, short for Alaska Utility Resilience and Optimization using Real-time AI, will use advanced artificial intelligence to improve electric power systems serving rural and coastal communities.
claims.source_outlet: University of Alaska Fairbanks
claims.notes: The page also states the award is part of the U.S. Department of Energy's Genesis Mission. Note for the ledger, this same UAF release was the source for deck No. 31 on August 12th, so the deck must not re-tell the AURORA-AI story, only cite the figure as a comparator.

claims.claim: Richard Wies, a professor at UAF, is principal investigator for the AURORA-AI project.
claims.verbatim: said ACEP's Richard Wies, principal investigator for the project and a professor at UAF.
claims.source_outlet: University of Alaska Fairbanks
claims.notes: ACEP is given on the page as the Alaska Center for Energy and Power. The verbatim is an attribution tag, so it reads as a fragment. No quotation by Wies is carried in this claim set, and the deck may therefore not put words in his mouth.

killed.claim: The NSF announcement of August 4th states the November 4, 2026 proposal deadline.
killed.why: The announcement page was fetched twice and searched explicitly for the word November. Returned NOT PRESENT both times. The deadline exists only on the solicitation, C06. Any slide pairing the deadline with the announcement URL would cite a page that does not carry it.

killed.claim: NSF 26-513 is a firm $100 million program.
killed.why: Downgraded rather than killed outright, see C10 and C11. The solicitation's Anticipated Funding Amount line says $40,000,000 to $100,000,000, so $100 million is the ceiling of a stated range and is the press release's figure. A flat assertion that NSF is spending $100 million is not supported by the solicitation.

killed.claim: The solicitation forbids Alaska or any applicant from adding its own money to enlarge a hub.
killed.why: Overstated by the showrunner's brief. The verified sentence, C05, is Inclusion of voluntary committed cost sharing is prohibited, which bars a proposer from pledging match INSIDE the proposal. It is routine NSF policy and it does not bar a state or a university from spending its own funds on compute. The deck's argument must rest on the accurate narrower version.

killed.claim: The solicitation names Tribal colleges or Alaska Native organizations as an eligible applicant category.
killed.why: The eligibility list was requested in full on a dedicated fetch and returned exactly two bullets, IHEs and non-profit non-academic organizations. A search for the word Tribal on the page returned NOT PRESENT. Neither the presence nor an explicit exclusion can be asserted.

killed.claim: Alaska has only one research university while other states have thirty, so the cap is unequal in practice.
killed.why: No page was fetched in this run that counts research universities per state. The thirty is a rhetorical number from the scout merge with no source behind it. The size argument must be carried by land area, C23 and C24, which is verified, and not by an institution count that is not.

killed.claim: The AIDEA parcel near Houston is intended for AI data centers or compute.
killed.why: The DNR notice as fetched describes a noncompetitive public and charitable use conveyance and does not state a compute or data center end use in any text returned across two fetches. Asserting the end use from this URL would misrepresent the primary document. The whole private-land contrast was dropped from the deck as a result.

killed.claim: The average hub award will be $10 million.
killed.why: Arithmetic that NSF does not state. $100,000,000 divided by 10 is $10,000,000, but the funding figure is a range, C11, and the award count is anticipated rather than fixed, C12, so the quotient is not a fact about any award. Retained only as an internal magnitude sanity check in the note on C12.

killed.claim: Alaska's total area is 665,384 square miles and that is the figure to compare against Rhode Island.
killed.why: Not killed for accuracy, the figure verified and reconciles, but excluded from use to prevent a unit mismatch. The deck uses LAND area on both sides of the ratio in C24. Mixing Alaska total area against Rhode Island land area would inflate the ratio to 643 and would be wrong.
